messages:
maureen: Quick note from today's bring-up: ptq-int8 reranker candidate for v4 shows overall NDCG@10 -1.7% but MRR -4.1%. the signal isn't uniform; a small subset of queries flips a lot.

devon: can you summarize the failing patterns?

maureen: sure. two clusters: 1) queries with HTML entities ( , &, ') and 2) percent-encoded URLs (eg. %2F, %20). each cluster is only ~2% of eval but MRR in-cluster is -9% and -13% respectively.

raj: interesting. any chance these were underrepresented in the onboarding holdout vs prod? dataset mismatch could amplify ptq sensitivity.

maureen: checked that: our sampled holdout had fewer percent-encoded urls (1.2% vs 3.9% in prod sample). i think selection + formatting differences matter. we also discovered our preprocessing decodes HTML entities in one pipeline but not the other, so tokenization diverges.

devon: ptq tends to be brittle when token id sequences change slightly. even HTML entity decoding -> different tokens can shift attention and nudge ranking for near-ties.

maureen: repro snippet:
```
raw = "How to fix error & folder structure %2Fhome%2Fuser%2Fapp"
pipeA: html_unescape -> tokenized -> model_float -> top1 A
pipeB: leave-escaped -> tokenized -> model_int8 -> top1 B
```

raj: two actionables: 1) add per-slice NDCG/MRR reporting in nightly for patterns `&[a-z]+;|%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}` 2) add a small anchor test in the onboarding checklist: ensure preprocessing canonicalization (either decode or consistently preserve) before tokenization for both eval and prod paths.

devon: also propose synthetic negative augmentation: add a small synthetic subset of percent-encoded and entity-heavy queries to the validation holdout used for quantization calibration. could help the PTQ optimizer see those patterns.

ci-bot: opened issue #3987: "entity + pct-encoded slices in ptq bench + canonicalization checklist" and kicked off extended holdout run: https://git.internal/r/3987

maureen: i'll add canonicalization to the onboarding doc and run a quick PTQ with tokenizer-locked artifacts and the synthetic-augmented holdout. will post numbers.

raj: when you post numbers, include slice-wise sample counts, NDCG@1/5/10 and MRR with 95% bootstrap CIs so product can weigh rollout.

maureen: good call. will do. thanks :thumbsup:
